fact: El Mouhassil was tested and provided to communes by the Direction Generale des Collectivites Territoriales of the Ministry of the Interior and Decentralisation, with partner support from Germany, France and the World Bank; undated, so the report date 2022-11 is used.

On 11 July 2023 the commune of Rosso held a training session on integrating civil-status records into its El Mouhassil programme, which the consultant describes as the programme for collecting and centralising municipal revenues; no figures are given.

On 23 May 2023 the commune of Zouerate launched its 'municipal collector' programme, a digitised tax collection programme built on a census of all commercial activities in the town; the report names no other commune and no counts.

The Zouerate mayor said the programme was launched in collaboration with the Territorial Directorate of Local Authorities of the Ministry of the Interior and Decentralisation; no budget line or plan is stated.

In Sebkha, a seven-week census of taxpayers found 10,564 taxpayers instead of the 2,000 officially recognised; the El Mouhassil software, launched in April 2019, issues numbered barcoded fiscal stamps, tracks each stamp from stock to sale to its payment into the commune's Treasury account, and 13 agents with tablets cover 16 sectors and scan each trader's stamp for paid, paid-this-month or overdue status.
The Sebkha mayor describes the system as completely independent, run by the commune with its own stamps; the trace is lost when the money enters the commune's account at the Public Treasury.

El Mouhassil is live in one commune, Sebkha (Nouakchott), since April 2019; eight others are installing it in April 2020: Tevragh Zeina, Timbedra, Nouadhibou, Boghé, Ksar, Toujounine, Arafat and Rosso; no national count of communes is given.
The commune's mayor defined the management processes and entrusted the build to a Mauritanian start-up; the commune runs the system and thanks German cooperation (GIZ) for technical expertise.
GIZ provided technical expertise to the commune for El Mouhassil; no commune budget line for it is stated.

Collection with the new secured fiscal stamps resumed in Sebkha in January 2020; the piece reports a 500 per cent rise in communal taxes between 2018 and 2020 and installation under way in eight more communes (April 2020).
